column1: # Forever's own areas, and which of them have an entry.
# Every column here comes from the game's own AreaTable, fetched as CSV from
# wago.tools, whose robots.txt permits exactly that route and blocks the HTML
# browser. Product "wowf", build 1.60.1.70862, read on 2026-11-08. The names
# are the client's own spelling, which is what Data/Schema.lua keys on.
# No notes column, for the same reason tools/characters.tsv has none: the one
# in places.tsv held three wrong notes and those errors reached finished lore.
# has_entry was produced by loading the addon against tools/mock_wow.lua,
# dumping every registered entry name through ns.EachEntry, and matching on a
# normalised name. That is a name match, not the resolver: a place whose entry
# exists but whose parent zone differs would show as having one. /ftn areas
# inside the game uses the real ns.FindZone / ns.FindSub / ns.FindInstance.
# The 47 have no entry because nothing describes them in any data that can be
# read from here. Checked on 2026-11-08, all via wago.tools, whose robots.txt
#   AreaTable          names and parents only, which is where these 47 came from
#   AreaPOI            372 rows, 150 with a description; 0 of the 47 appear, and
#                      the descriptions are UI strings like "Alliance Controlled"
#   Map                no description set for any of the four zones
#   QuestV2            exists, but carries no text columns at all
#   Achievement        495 rows; the zones are named, none of the 47 are
# The pattern is consistent and it explains itself: what describes a place in
# this game is quest text and NPC dialogue, and both live on the server. The
# client ships the names and not the words.
# That is NOT the same as "no lore exists". warcraft.wiki.gg has Forever
# coverage, 259 pages tagged "Added in patch 1.60.1" when last counted, and
# Wowhead has a /forever/ section. Both disallow this tooling's user agents, so
# a person with a browser can read what this cannot. The game itself is the
# other source, and the better one.
# /ftn areas does the has_entry check from inside the game, for the whole world
